title: New Drug Offers Hope for Millions with High Blood Pressure
subtitle: Recent research suggests a new medication could provide long-term relief for patients with a specific type of hypertension.

summary.en: A new drug called baxdrostat is showing surprising results for patients with high blood pressure. While most blood pressure medications must be taken daily for life, this drug appears to provide benefits for years after treatment stops. The medication works by targeting a hormone that causes the body to hold onto too much salt. Experts believe this could change how doctors treat a common form of the condition. Larger studies are currently underway to confirm these findings.
summary.zh: 一種名為 baxdrostat 的新藥對高血壓患者展現出驚人的療效。雖然大多數降血壓藥物必須終身每日服用，但這種藥物似乎在停止治療後仍能持續發揮效益。該藥物的作用機制是針對一種會導致身體滯留過多鹽分的荷爾蒙。專家認為，這可能會改變醫生治療此類常見疾病的方式。目前更大規模的研究正在進行中，以確認這些發現。

paragraphs.en: Millions of people around the world live with high blood pressure, a condition that often requires daily medication for the rest of a patient's life. However, new research published in the New England Journal of Medicine suggests that a different future may be possible. A drug called baxdrostat has shown the potential to reverse a common cause of high blood pressure, with some patients remaining healthy even two years after they stopped taking the daily pills.
paragraphs.zh: 全球有數百萬人患有高血壓，這種疾病通常需要患者終身每日服藥。然而，發表在《新英格蘭醫學雜誌》(New England Journal of Medicine) 上的最新研究顯示，未來或許會有不同的可能。一種名為 baxdrostat 的藥物展現出逆轉常見高血壓成因的潛力，部分患者在停止每日服藥後，甚至能維持兩年的健康狀態。

paragraphs.en: This development is particularly welcome news in the medical community, especially following recent disappointments in cardiovascular research. As reported by The Guardian Health, other new drugs designed to prevent heart disease recently failed to show the expected benefits in clinical trials. In contrast, the findings regarding baxdrostat offer a more positive outlook for patients struggling with hypertension, which is the medical term for high blood pressure.
paragraphs.zh: 這項進展對醫學界而言是特別令人欣喜的消息，尤其是在近期心血管研究頻頻受挫之後。據《衛報健康版》(The Guardian Health) 報導，其他旨在預防心臟病的新藥近期在臨床試驗中未能展現預期效益。相比之下，關於 baxdrostat 的研究結果為那些受高血壓（醫學術語為 hypertension）困擾的患者提供了更樂觀的前景。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian Health, the drug targets a specific cause of hypertension known as primary aldosteronism. This condition occurs in about 5 to 10 percent of cases and is caused by small growths on the adrenal glands. These growths lead the body to produce too much of a hormone called aldosterone, which signals the kidneys to keep more salt in the body, thereby raising blood pressure. Currently, the standard treatment for this condition is surgery to remove the affected gland, but this is not always a complete cure.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報健康版》報導，該藥物針對的是一種稱為原發性醛固酮增多症 (primary aldosteronism) 的高血壓特定成因。這種情況約佔病例的百分之五至十，是由腎上腺上的小腫塊所引起。這些腫塊會導致身體產生過多的醛固酮 (aldosterone) 荷爾蒙，向腎臟發出訊號以保留更多鹽分，進而導致血壓升高。目前，針對此症的標準治療方式是手術切除受影響的腺體，但這並不總是能徹底治癒。

paragraphs.en: Professor Morris Brown, a specialist at Queen Mary University of London who led the study, described the results as very exciting. In a small trial involving 14 patients, those who took the drug for six to 12 months saw their blood pressure improve significantly. Most surprisingly, when doctors checked on these patients up to two years later, their blood pressure remained at healthy levels. In fact, nearly a quarter of the patients were able to stop all other treatments entirely.
paragraphs.zh: 領導這項研究的倫敦瑪麗女王大學 (Queen Mary University of London) 專家莫里斯·布朗 (Morris Brown) 教授形容研究結果令人振奮。在一項涉及十四名患者的小型試驗中，服用該藥物六至十二個月的患者，其血壓狀況顯著改善。最令人驚訝的是，當醫生在兩年後追蹤這些患者時，他們的血壓仍維持在健康水平。事實上，近四分之一的患者能夠完全停止所有其他治療。

paragraphs.en: Experts believe the drug works by suppressing the hormone that raises blood pressure. Professor Brown suggests that by stopping the production of this hormone, the drug may actually destroy the specific cells that cause the problem. He notes that this theory is based on earlier experiments and is currently being tested further in laboratory settings to confirm exactly how the drug changes the body over time.
paragraphs.zh: 專家認為，該藥物的作用機制在於抑制導致血壓升高的荷爾蒙。布朗教授推測，透過停止這種荷爾蒙的產生，該藥物或許能真正破壞導致問題的特定細胞。他指出，這項理論基於早期的實驗，目前正在實驗室環境中進行進一步測試，以確認該藥物隨時間推移對身體造成的確切影響。

paragraphs.en: While these results are promising, medical professionals are urging caution. Mason Freeman, a professor of medicine at Harvard University who was involved in the study, noted that it is still too early to declare these patients fully cured. He explained that a larger trial is necessary to see if these effects are common among a wider group of people. If the results remain consistent in larger studies, it could change how doctors diagnose and treat patients, potentially allowing them to avoid invasive procedures like surgery.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管這些結果充滿希望，但醫學界人士仍呼籲謹慎看待。參與該研究的哈佛大學 (Harvard University) 醫學教授梅森·弗里曼 (Mason Freeman) 指出，現在斷言這些患者已完全康復還為時過早。他解釋說，需要進行更大規模的試驗，才能觀察這些效果是否在更廣泛的人群中普遍存在。如果結果在大型研究中保持一致，這可能會改變醫生診斷和治療患者的方式，並可能讓患者免於手術等侵入性治療。

paragraphs.en: Baxdrostat has already been approved in the United States for patients whose high blood pressure is not controlled by existing medications. In the United Kingdom, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice) is currently assessing the drug. If the assessment is successful, the medication could become available through the National Health Service (NHS) as early as next year.
paragraphs.zh: Baxdrostat 已在美國獲准用於現有藥物無法控制高血壓的患者。在英國，國家健康與照顧卓越研究院 (National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, Nice) 目前正在評估該藥物。如果評估順利，該藥物最快可能於明年透過國家醫療保健服務 (National Health Service, NHS) 提供給民眾使用。

paragraphs.en: For now, the medical community is watching the progress of this drug closely. If baxdrostat continues to show such long-term success, it could represent a major shift in how we manage chronic conditions. Instead of simply managing symptoms with daily pills, doctors might one day offer treatments that provide a lasting solution for millions of people worldwide.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，醫學界正密切關注該藥物的進展。如果 baxdrostat 能持續展現如此長期的成效，這可能代表我們管理慢性病的方式將出現重大轉變。醫生未來或許不再只是透過每日服藥來控制症狀，而是能提供為全球數百萬人帶來持久解決方案的治療方式。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To change something to the opposite of what it was before.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此處指將病情「逆轉」回健康狀態，而非單純的「倒車」。文中：A drug called baxdrostat has shown the potential to reverse a common cause of high blood pressure, with some patients remaining healthy even two years after they stopped taking the daily pills.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To direct an action or effect towards a specific object or goal.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（目標），這裡作動詞，指藥物「針對」特定病因。文中：According to The Guardian Health, the drug targets a specific cause of hypertension known as primary aldosteronism.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To control or keep a condition under control, often through regular treatment.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指對慢性病的「控制」，而非一般的「經營」或「處理」。文中：Instead of simply managing symptoms with daily pills, doctors might one day offer treatments that provide a lasting solution for millions of people worldwide.

previousArticles.title: New Heart Disease Drugs Fail to Show Expected Benefits
previousArticles.summaryEn: Researchers recently tested two new drugs designed to prevent heart disease. Despite high hopes, both medications failed to reduce the number of heart attacks or strokes in patients. One drug targeted inflammation, while the other focused on a specific protein in the blood. Experts are now working to understand why these treatments did not work as expected. The findings highlight the complexity of treating advanced heart disease.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the primary mechanism by which primary aldosteronism leads to high blood pressure?

options.A: The adrenal glands fail to produce enough hormones to regulate blood flow.
options.B: Small growths cause an excess of aldosterone, resulting in the kidneys retaining more salt.
options.C: The drug baxdrostat creates an imbalance in the chemical signals sent to the kidneys.
options.D: Patients consume too much salt in their daily diet, which the kidneys cannot filter properly.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，primary aldosteronism 是由腎上腺上的小增生物（small growths）引起，導致身體產生過多的 aldosterone，進而促使腎臟保留過多的鹽分，導致血壓升高。選項 A 與文意相反；選項 C 錯誤，因為該機制是疾病本身造成的，而非藥物；選項 D 文中並未提及患者飲食習慣與此病症的直接因果關係。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the future of surgical treatments for hypertension if baxdrostat's success continues?

options.A: Surgery will become the only way to permanently cure hypertension.
options.B: Surgery will be required for all patients who do not respond to daily pills.
options.C: Surgical procedures might become less necessary as a standard treatment option.
options.D: Surgery will be replaced by a combination of daily medication and lifestyle changes.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第六段，Mason Freeman 教授提到如果大規模試驗結果一致，可能會改變醫生診斷和治療患者的方式，並「potentially allowing them to avoid invasive procedures like surgery」（可能讓患者避免手術等侵入性治療）。這暗示手術作為目前標準治療的必要性將會降低。選項 A 與文意完全相反；選項 B 與 D 皆未在文中提到是必然趨勢。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'managing' mean in the context of 'managing symptoms with daily pills'?

options.A: Controlling or keeping symptoms under check without necessarily curing the underlying cause.
options.B: Organizing the schedule of a patient's medication intake.
options.C: Successfully eliminating the root cause of a chronic disease.
options.D: Supervising the medical staff who prescribe the treatment to patients.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境中，managing 指的是透過藥物來「控制」或「減輕」症狀，而非根治（cure）。文章最後一段將這種「管理症狀」與「提供持久解決方案（lasting solution）」做對比，暗示管理只是權宜之計。選項 B 僅指行政上的安排；選項 C 指的是治療目標而非現狀；選項 D 則完全偏離了醫學治療的語境。

quiz.question: What is the central message of this article regarding the drug baxdrostat?

options.A: Baxdrostat is a proven cure that has already replaced all other forms of hypertension treatment.
options.B: While initial results are promising, the drug is currently only available for patients in the UK.
options.C: New research suggests baxdrostat could shift hypertension treatment from symptom management to a potential long-term solution.
options.D: The medical community is skeptical about the drug's effectiveness due to a lack of laboratory testing.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章的核心在於介紹 baxdrostat 這項新研究，強調它不僅能控制血壓，甚至可能提供長期解決方案，這對慢性病管理是一大轉變。選項 A 過於誇大，文中提到仍需大規模試驗；選項 B 錯誤，因為該藥物已在美國獲准；選項 D 錯誤，因為文中提到醫學界持「謹慎樂觀」態度，而非完全懷疑，且實驗室測試正在進行中。
